summary: # CLO Skills Workshop - Onion Quilting Production Techniques Guide ## Introduction Today, we are going to make a drawing of an onion line. In this workshop, you'll learn how to create an onion line using CLO software. ## Drawing the Onion Line ### Step 1: Create the Rectangle First, we draw a rectangle with a ruler. The length and width can be decided by yourself. ### Step 2: Draw the Inner Line Next, we draw an inner line in the middle. The length of the inner line is 15 cm. We click on it and right-click. Then, we can enter its length and click OK. Double-click to end. ### Step 3: Adding Small Lines We can make small lines on the top of the line. The length of the inner line can be made into a triangle. We may also draw a rectangle with a slightly larger line. Then, divide the inner line into two. After the division is made, the inner line is divided into two. ### Step 4: Repeat the Process Now, we will repeat the same process. We draw two lines on the top of the line. The length here can be adjusted to 5 mm. Then, click on all, and the left and right are available, and then click to confirm. After it is generated, there will be a basic line above. You can delete the basic line and select it. ### Step 5: Generating Vertical Lines Because I don't need a basic line, I can delete it, and we can also generate a vertical line at the same point. This vertical line is aligned to the Y-axis, and then we set the angle to 45 degrees. Click on all, left and right, and then delete the basic line again. ## Adjusting the Shape of the Onion ### Step 6: Draw Vertical Y-Axis Next, let’s repeat it again. The vertical line will be to the Y-axis, and the angle is 90 degrees because I want a vertical Y-axis. Set the length to 5 mm, and then select all options, including left and right. ### Step 7: Adjusting the Onion Shape After drawing like this, we are going to adjust the shape of the onion. First, draw it with the internal line and connect it. If I accidentally press the mouse button, it may create a curve if it is not long enough. If I don't want this kind of curve, then press Esc to exit and click directly. Just pull it over, double-shift, and finish. ### Step 8: Correcting Curves Because of the meniscus effect, if you press the mouse button and left-click, it will pull out a curve. When you press the mouse button and left-click and don’t release it, you will pull out a curve. To exit it, press Esc. ### Step 9: Adjust the Curve Shape Next, I want to adjust the shape of this curve. You can use the click curve point or click circle. Here, I use the click curve point to adjust its shape. If you want the shape to be similar to the desired outcome, place the mouse here, and then you can add this pattern to it. Then, adjust the size to be similar using the click curve tool. ### Step 10: Final Adjustments You may want to make it a little bigger or a little smaller. It's nearly the same now. You can continue to use the click curve tool to adjust its shape. Adjust slowly, adding or reducing points as necessary. If this looks good, you can proceed. ### Step 11: Deleting Patterns If you want to delete this pattern, right-click and rewrite it. After adjustment, we can use the edit stages to select this line. Right-click to find the option for "copy as mirror," and select the mirror line you want to mirror. ## Finalizing the Onion Line ### Step 12: Mirroring Lines Select the lines you want to mirror, and you will see the changes. It should look good. You can then select these four lines and right-click to copy the inner line of the mirror and select the basic line of the mirror. ### Step 13: Framing the Onion The upper line can be resolved in this way. When framing it, you can delete the unnecessary lines first. If there are empty points, which indicate broken points, you can select them. Right-click and merge the refraction points with it. Then, right-click to convert it to a free line point. ### Step 14: Copying and Pasting After converting it to a free line point, select between these two lines and right-click to copy. When pasting, press the Shift key. You can enter a specific size, for example, 100 mm for the next circle. Click OK. ### Step 15: Final Touches You can also copy the top and bottom. Use the right-click to paste and press the Shift key. Enter 300 for the circle size and confirm. Repeat this process to complete the onion horizontal line. If you want to overlap points, you can do so by clicking the mouse button. Verify the desired values, and click OK. ### Conclusion Now, the onion line is complete, and it should appear gray. This concludes the production of our onion aerial string. Thank you for watching!
